_comment: A bare ESP32-S3 push-to-talk button isn't a new agent - it's a physical node that gets bound to whichever agent should answer it (e.g. the existing 'claude' front-door agent on Pyramid). Every new board goes through this same two-step pairing before its talk.ptt.* commands are honored - see docs/voice-interface-2026-09-13.md and docs/gateway-crash-loop-2026-09-23.md's gateway/pairing source.
steps: 1. Flash the board so it calls talk.ptt.start/stop and talk.speak against Pyramid's gateway URL.
2. openclaw devices list                     # find the new device's pending request
4. openclaw nodes pending                    # find its capability/command request
6. openclaw nodes rename --node <id> --name "<a real name, e.g. kitchen-button>"
